factual_errors.claim: Framing DH-485 incompatibility as a config/wiring problem to troubleshoot rather than the definitive fix
factual_errors.why_wrong: DH-485 requires token-passing arbitration and a TX-EN control line a transparent converter structurally cannot provide; no amount of baud/parity/termination checking will fix it. The correct answer is to reinstall the protocol-aware interface or an equivalent (1747-AIC, 1761-NET-AIC), not to keep tuning the transparent converter.

factual_errors.claim: No mention of voltage mismatch risk
factual_errors.why_wrong: DH-485 RJ45 uses 0-5V RS-485 levels, not Ethernet voltages; connecting standard Ethernet gear to that port risks damaging the network card or processor. This is an equipment-damage hazard the answer never raises.

notes: Core diagnosis (transparent converter can't speak DH-485) is directionally right, but zero manual grounding (general_reasoning, no citations) and the specific troubleshooting steps are presented with unwarranted confidence. Buries the actual fix (replace with protocol-aware interface) as a conditional rather than stating it. Omits the voltage-damage warning entirely. Fails correctness and evidence thresholds.
